title: SIMBENCH: BENCHMARKING THE ABILITY OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS TO SIMULATE HUMAN BEHAVIORS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance from human ground truth) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on religious affiliation and religiosity/practice, compared to the general population.

Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on political affiliation and ideology, compared to the general population.

Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on income, social standing, employment status, and education, compared to the general population.

Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on domicile and urbanicity (e.g., urban vs. rural), compared to the general population.

Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on marital status, compared to the general population.

Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on age brackets, compared to the general population.
Measuring the degradation in group-level simulation accuracy (using Total Variation Distance) when prompting models to simulate populations conditioned on gender, compared to the general population.
